question.value: How do linear carbon chains (polyynes and cyanopolyynes) form and grow in the envelope of the C-star IRC +10216, and where are they located radially?

evidence.quote: We have carried out a combined observational and modeling study of the formation of carbon chains in the C-star envelope IRC +10216
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00432.S.
A $\lambda~3$ mm spectral survey of IRC +10216 covering the frequency range 84.0-115.5 GHz was carried out with ALMA band 3 during Cycle 2.

evidence.quote: stacked the maps of a selected list of 19 lines, all free of blending and observed with a sufficient quality

method.value: Strip at PA=45 deg and azimuthal averages of maps

analysis_steps.goal: Chemical model of the expanding envelope

method.value: Gas-phase kinetic model, isotropic expansion from 2e14 cm, UV illumination by Draine field, NH/AV reduced 1.5x, cosmic ray rate 1.2e-17 s-1

evidence.quote: The adopted cosmic-ray ionization rate of H$_2$ is $1.2\times10^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Distance 123 pc; C2H2 and HCN abundances 8e-5 and 4e-5 relative to H2

evidence.quote: the adopted abundances relative to H$_2$ are $8\times10^{-5}$ and $4\times10^{-5}$, respectively

fitting.value: No fit; NH/AV tuned to reproduce observed radial location

evidence.loc: Model, Chemical model: formation of carbon chains
evidence.quote: For the purpose of reproducing the observed radial location of carbon chains, we have adopted a $N_{\rm H}$ / $A_V$ ratio 1.5 times lower than the canonical interstellar value

findings_qualitative.value: HC3N appears earlier (from ~7 arcsec) and CN extends beyond 30 arcsec

evidence.quote: The radial distribution of CN is also markedly different from the rest of the species as it extends out to radial distances beyond 30$''$.

claims.hypothesis: Carbon chains are confined to the outer envelope with radial stratification dependent on species
claims.experiment: ALMA+IRAM 30m maps of seven species at ~1 arcsec
claims.result: Hollow shells at 10-20 arcsec composed of thin non-concentric arcs; hydrocarbons co-located, cyanides diverse

evidence.quote: indicating that the mass loss process has been discontinuous and not fully isotropic

claims.hypothesis: UV-driven gas-phase growth explains observed chain distributions
claims.experiment: Chemical + LVG radiative transfer model compared with radial profiles
claims.result: Model reasonably reproduces observations except HC5N onset
claims.finding: Polyynes grow via C2H/C4H reactions, cyanopolyynes via CN/C3N with polyynes

evidence.quote: This behavior is reasonably well reproduced by our chemical model

limitations_admitted.value: Spherical isotropic model cannot reproduce arcs; comparison only first order; IR pumping uncertain for C4H, C6H, C3N

evidence.quote: the comparison between the calculated and observed emission distributions can only be done to first order, and not at the sub-arcsecond level
